organiser.name: Kiwiburn Incorporated Society (volunteer-run Burning Man regional event)

attendance.note: Press figure: event 'attended by about 2400 people' (NZ Herald/Whanganui Chronicle, Google snippet; article covers the January 2025 burn, year inferred from coverage timing). Organiser FAQ says 2025 numbers were increased to 2450 and the event is heavily oversubscribed; organiser 2020 census gives a population of 1,995.

audience.age_range: Mostly 22 to 35 (2020 census: largest bands 29 to 35, then 22 to 28)
audience.psychographics: Participatory Burning Man community with no spectators; top draws are community, self-expression and art; respondents mostly from Auckland and Wellington; 37% first-timers in 2020.

add_sources.note: 'The ticket price includes your automatic annual membership subscription to Kiwiburn Incorporated Society'; 'a festival run entirely by volunteers'.
'The numbers for Kiwiburn 2025 have been increased to 2450, of which 450 will be available via the lottery, however the event is still heavily oversubscribed'.

Read via WebFetch (PDF): gender Female 50.59%, Male 43.73%, Other 5.69%; age bars peak at 29 to 35 and 22 to 28; first time 37%; top attractions Community, Self expression, Art; most respondents from Auckland and Wellington. Newest census on the site is 2020.
Contact form with a 'Media Liaison' option for media enquiries; no email or partnership route.

add_gaps: Commerce-free event under Burning Man's Decommodification principle; no sponsors and brand activations unlikely to be accepted
Audience data is from the 2020 census; no newer census published
No partnerships contact; contact form only (Media Liaison option)
notes: Kiwiburn's homepage states the Decommodification principle: environments 'unmediated by commercial sponsorships, transactions, or advertising', and the FAQ says it is a commerce-free event (only ice is sold). Treat as not partnerable for High Ground; any presence would have to be gifted participation by people, not branding. A third-party blog says 2026 tickets cost $300 (Google snippet, https://www.furrociousfurr.com/blogs/news/what-to-expect-at-kiwiburn-nz-festival-style-in-the-land-of-the-long-white-cloud), not confirmed on kiwiburn.com, so ticket_price left unset.
